definition: Alice AI is a neural network family developed by the Russian company Yandex LLC.
details: Alice AI can create and revise texts, generate new ideas and capture the context of the conversation with the user. Alice AI is trained using a dataset which includes information from books, magazines, newspapers and other open sources available on the internet. The neural network may get facts wrong and hallucinate, but as it learns, it will produce increasingly accurate answers.

explainer.lead: Alice AI is Yandex's family of generative models for working with language, combining vision and language, and creating images. It powers the Alice AI assistant and features in Yandex services, including generative answers in Search, while business users can access Yandex language models through Yandex Cloud.

tiers.eli5: Alice AI is like a team of three digital makers: one writes and answers, one works with pictures and words, and one draws pictures. You might ask it to draft a story and then say, “Make it shorter and funnier,” and it can use the conversation so far to revise it. It can still make mistakes, so its answers need checking.
tiers.practitioner: The family is applied through the Alice AI assistant, Yandex Search, and Yandex's business model APIs. Earlier integrations used YandexGPT for text generation and structuring, business chatbots, video retellings, and posts in Shedevrum; access has been provided through the Yandex Cloud API and AI Studio API, with a Playground offered for testing. Outputs can contain factual errors or hallucinations, and YandexGPT 5 Lite Instruct uses a custom licence rather than a standard open-source one.
tiers.paperLevel: Alice AI is a generative model family comprising a language model (Alice AI LLM), a vision–language model (Alice AI VLM), and an image-generation model (Alice AI Art). The technical report published on 11 December 2025 states that Alice AI LLM training was initialised with Qwen3-235B weights. Related releases include mixture-of-experts models with many total parameters but far fewer active per token; like other generative language models, they can produce incorrect facts and hallucinations.

explainer.example: A user asks the assistant to draft an announcement for a community book sale, then follows up with “make it warmer and add that entry is free.” The language model can use the conversation's context to revise the announcement, but the user should check details such as the date and location before publishing it.

usedIn.name: Alice AI assistant
usedIn.detail: Uses the models for conversational assistance, following YandexGPT's earlier integration into the Alice virtual assistant.

usedIn.name: Yandex Search
usedIn.detail: Provides generative answers; a fine-tuned Alice AI Search model had also been used there since July 2026.

usedIn.name: Shedevrum
usedIn.detail: YandexGPT was added in June 2023 to help users create posts with a title, text, and illustration.

usedIn.name: Yandex Cloud
usedIn.detail: Gives business customers API access to Yandex language models for applications such as assistants, chatbots, and text generation.

components.name: Alice AI LLM: the family's language model.
Alice AI VLM: its vision–language model.
Alice AI Art: its image-generation model.
Yandex services and Cloud APIs: places where the models are delivered to users and businesses.

flow: A user supplies a request, such as a question, writing task, or image prompt.
The relevant model handles language, vision and language, or image generation.
The model generates a response, which can be revised as the conversation continues.
The result reaches users through Alice AI, Yandex services, or business API access.
explainer.origin: Yandex introduced the Alice AI family on 28 October 2025, following its YaLM and YandexGPT work. A technical report published on 11 December 2025 described the family's development.
explainer.whyItMatters: The family brings text, vision–language, and image generation under one Yandex product line and connects them to consumer services and business tools. Its releases also show a progression from earlier YandexGPT models to newer open-weight and mixture-of-experts models.
